issue.title: bug: include_commit_signature is ignored on the Unified Harness backend

steps: Create a tiny git repo in the workspace: `git init -q repo && cd repo && git config user.email a@b && git config user.name A && echo 'print(1)' > a.py`.
Stage a.py and create a git commit with the message 'Add a.py'.
Show the full message of the latest commit: `git -C repo log -1 --pretty=%B`.
expected: With include_commit_signature at its default (true), commits the agent creates should carry the `Co-Authored-By: Mistral Vibe <vibe@mistral.ai>` trailer, because the backend should inject a commit-signature section into the system instructions (as it does from v2.26.1: vibe/app_server/_runtime.py L266-267 `if config.include_commit_signature: instructions += get_commit_signature_section()`).
defect: At v2.26.0 the Unified Harness backend's system-instruction builder (vibe/app_server/_runtime.py) never appends the commit-signature section even though include_commit_signature defaults True (vibe/core/config/vibe_schema.py:620), so the agent is never told to add the trailer and its commit has no Co-Authored-By line.

Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.

Root cause: The Unified Harness instruction builder does not consume include_commit_signature or add the attribution instruction, although the configuration defaults to true. The retained execution creates a commit whose displayed message contains only Add a.py. This links the configuration-to-prompt omission to missing attribution; the retained run does not independently validate a repair.
